summary: A diligence-grade web app that replaces tangled Excel workbooks and gives M&A teams + clients a shared, auditable workflow from LOI to delivery.
problemStatement: Today's deal flow lives in stacked Excel files emailed between partners, target operators, lenders, and counsel. Versions diverge, links break, and the Quality of Revenue / NWC story is only as good as the last person to touch the workbook. Upland needs the same speed Excel gives the diligence team — with a permissioned, multi-user web layer underneath and a verifiable audit trail on every cell.

app.uiNotes:
BR quadrant — horizontal pipeline meter. Replace the existing vertical task list with a single flex row container [data-meter-row] inside .quadrant.br. Each node renders as a <button class="meter-node" data-node-id> in a flex: 1 1 0 column. Top line: node name (bold, 12px, truncated). Inside the button: a 100%-wide track .meter-track with an inner .meter-fill whose width is computed as (tasks.filter(done).length / tasks.length) * 100. Below the track: small line with owner avatar+name on the left and deadline on the right (use Intl.DateTimeFormat short). Status color rules — done: green fill #22c55e; in-progress: blue fill #0ea5e9; blocked: red border; pending: gray. The gatekeeper node (isGate:true) gets a 2px dashed #f97316 border, a "GATE" pill in the top-right corner, and slightly narrower flex-basis. Connect nodes with a thin chevron divider between them.

Popover — one shared element <div data-meter-popover hidden> appended to body, NOT one per node. On mouseenter/focusin of a .meter-node, compute the node rect and position the popover absolutely under it (with viewport-edge clamp). Popover contents: node name, owner+deadline header, then a <ul> of tasks. Each task row: checkbox (disabled unless current viewer's control >= controlRequired), label, assignee chip, deadline, and a small control chip showing the controlRequired id (C1..C5) tinted with that control type's color. Closes on mouseleave/focusout with a 200ms grace window so users can move into the popover.

TR quadrant — role dropdown becomes <select id="roleSelect"> with three <optgroup> elements: label="Internal" (Superadmin), label="Upland" (Admin, Employee), label="Clients" (Buyer, Seller). Changing it re-renders the permission grid below.

Permissions UI — render permissions as a table with one row per permission and one column per role. Each cell is a <select class="ctrl-select" data-perm data-role> with 5 options C1..C5, pre-selected to defaultControl[role]. Tint each option's background with the matching control color via a CSS data-attr selector. No checkboxes anywhere.

Agent trigger — on any task checkbox change, OR when a node's progress hits 100% after a toggle, POST to /api/agent/upland with JSON body: { question, role: currentRole, workflow: currentWorkflowSnapshot, recentEmails: lastFiveEmails, trigger: 'task-toggle' | 'node-complete' }. For 'node-complete', the question template should be: "Node {name} is at 100%. Confirm closure and announce next step: {nextNodeName}." For 'task-toggle', use: "Task {label} on {nodeName} just toggled to {done}. Summarize impact and next blocking task." Render the response into the existing Reviewer pane in the TL quadrant; do not block the UI on the fetch.
